images.caption: View of a historic religious procession during the 2018 Heiligdomsvaart ("Relics Pilgrimage") in Maastricht, Netherlands. The history of this seven-yearly catholic pilgrimage goes back to the Middle Ages. The first 'modern' version took place in 1874. On both Sundays of the 10-day festival, a procession is held in which the main relics of the town and other devotional objects are exhibited. This photo was taken from the spectator stand in Vrijthof square at the end of the (second) procession on 3 June 2018. The marching band that closes the procession is Harmonie Sint Petrus en Paulus from the Maastricht neighbourhood and parish of Wolder.
images.alt: View of a historic religious procession during the 2018 Heiligdomsvaart ("Relics Pilgrimage") in Maastricht, Netherlands. images.caption:
I was thinking about how networks of processors work - while sitting having a beer in Maastricht. These notes are circa 1991.
At the time, I was working with Transputer based systems.  The transputer was  a microprocessor architecture of the 1980s, featuring integrated memory and serial communication links, intended for parallel computing. It was designed and produced by Inmos. We programmed these in occam  a concurrent programming language.

images.caption: Maastricht, the Netherlands. View towards the East of Plein 1992, the main square of the Céramique neighbourhood on the East bank of the river Meuse, named after the Treaty of Maastricht (1992). The square was designed in the late 1990s by Dutch architect Jo Coenen, as well as several buildings around it, including the Centre Céramique library on the right. To the left: part of La Résidence by Swiss architect Aurelio Galfetti and French architect Yann Keromnes. At the far end: a fragment of La Fortezza by Mario Botta.
images.alt: Maastricht, the Netherlands.
